newsitem.title: USA: Nike fourth-quarter results set record.
newsitem.headline: Nike fourth-quarter results set record.

text.p: Nike Inc. Tuesday reported a record fiscal fourth-quarter profit despite earlier warnings by the Beaverton, Ore.-based athletic apparel maker that sales and earnings would be below expectations.

Nike earned $155.8 million, or 52 cents a share, within the range forecast more than a month ago. Its latest results were up from $133.7 million, or 45 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose 28 percent to $2.37 billion from $1.85 billion.

In May, the company had forecast profits for the three months ended in May of between 51 cents and 56 cents a share, reflecting a shift in Europe to more advanced ordering, a shortage of apparel inventories and some cancellations in the United States.

Despite the reduced expectations, Nike Chairman and Chief Executive Philip Knight said fiscal 1997 was a record year for the company and, based on future order rates for the June to November period, Nike expects another year of record profits and revenues in fiscal 1998.
Nike said worldwide futures orders for delivery between June and November, a key indicator of demand, rose 18 percent to $4.9 billion.
